title: 2.1.40 A2.1.2 — Conditionals Checkpoint Quiz
description: Short written quiz on === vs ==, operator precedence, and tracing conditional code. AI-graded with hints.
sourceRef: designed — capstone quiz, assignment code A2.1.2 per curriculum-plan §2.1 Assignments; questions draw on book 2.1 Problem Set 2.1.7-2.1.10 intent (=== vs ==, operator precedence, trace prediction)

rubric.title: Q1: === vs == explained with an example
rubric.description: Student states that === checks both value and type (strict equality) while == converts types before comparing (loose equality), and gives a concrete example where the two disagree (e.g. 5 === "5" is false but 5 == "5" is true). Credit any correct example with the same shape.

rubric.title: Q2: Correctly identifies && runs before || and explains the parentheses
rubric.description: Student correctly states that && has higher precedence than || (so && runs first), and explains that adding parentheses around the && part makes the grouping explicit for a reader without changing the result. Deny if the order is reversed or no reasoning is given.

rubric.title: Q3 Snippet A: correctly traces the else if chain
rubric.description: Student says Snippet A logs 'Cold' (45 is not < 32, but is < 60) and explains that the chain checks conditions top to bottom and stops at the first true one.

rubric.title: Q3 Snippet B: correctly traces the chained ternary
rubric.description: Student says Snippet B logs 'C' (72 is not >= 90 or >= 80, but is >= 70) and explains the chained ternary is evaluated the same way as an else if chain.

rubric.title: Q3 Snippet C: correctly traces the OR string-literal trap
rubric.description: Student says Snippet C logs 'true' and explains that the right side of || is the bare string "Sunday", which is truthy on its own regardless of what day is set to — not a real comparison against day.
